metadata.note: The St. Paul and Duluth Railroad (1877-1900), its predecessor the Lake Superior and Mississippi (1870-1877) and the Northern Pacific successor era (1900-1967), as separate operator features sharing identical geometry where the same line changed hands; plus two later tourist operations on the road's track (the Lake Superior and Mississippi heritage railroad at Duluth and the Minnesota Zephyr at Stillwater) and Amtrak's North Star over the ex-St. P&D Grassy Point line. Drawn spans follow the research report's drawable: fields exactly. Research report: research/branches/st_paul_and_duluth_railroad.txt.
metadata.operator_split: Rule 4 splits: 1877 LS&M -> St. P&D reorganization (new company; lsm-st-paul-duluth vs stpd-*); 1900 NP purchase (stpd-st-paul-thomson / np-st-paul-carlton, stpd-duluth-short-line / np-duluth-short-line, stpd-grassy-point-line / np-grassy-point-line, stpd-taylors-falls-branch / np-taylors-falls-branch). The 1872 NP lease of the LS&M is NOT split: whether NP ran the trains is unproven (see not_yet_sourced). No BN split: the last NP passenger trains here ended 4 Jan 1967. Colours: Northern Pacific and Amtrak reuse their existing hexes, pulled programmatically from data/; LS&M #6B4423, St. P&D #C2571A, the heritage Lake Superior Transportation Club #5B7F95 and Minnesota Zephyr #9E2A55 are new, and a script confirmed no other company in data/ uses any of them.
branches_deliberately_omitted: Fond du Lac local remnant (West Duluth Jct - New Duluth - Fond du Lac) after 1888: no confirmable passenger year (report block [6], drawable NONE).

Minneapolis branch (Minneapolis and Duluth RR, East Minneapolis - White Bear): 1875 anchor only, and the operator (LS&M, M&D or M&StL) is unresolved, so Rule 4 cannot be satisfied (report block [13] recommends not drawing).
Stillwater branch in the LS&M and St. P&D eras, Grantsburg branch in the St. P&D era (opened 1884), Cloquet branch before 1942: lines were operated but no passenger year is confirmed.
Banning quarry spur (1892-1918): no passenger evidence.
Freight-only afterlives (Maplewood - Hugo Minnesota Commercial, North Branch - Hinckley St. Croix Valley RR 'Skally Line', White Bear - Stillwater after its unknown passenger end): Rule 1.
The 'Hinckley - Superior cutoff' is the Great Northern's Eastern Railway of Minnesota, not this road.
not_yet_sourced: OPEN ENDS: np-duluth-short-line ends 1951 [OPEN] (Jan 1951 Guide; conflicting second-hand claim of an Oct 1949 end; trains 65/66's route into Duluth to Jan 1967 unknown). np-taylors-falls-branch 1900-1902 [OPEN] (regular service ended between 1902 and 1948). np-cloquet-branch 1942 [OPEN] - 1951 [OPEN]. stpd-thomson-fond-du-lac-duluth ends 1886 as the last confirmed year (through trains moved to the Short Line 1886-88). lstc-west-duluth-boy-scout-landing 2026 [OPEN] (2023-2025 seasons likely, undated).

ANCHORS (one proven year; service certainly wider): stpd-grassy-point-line 1888, np-grassy-point-line 1951, np-stillwater-branch 1915, np-taylors-falls-branch 1948 (farewell run), np-grantsburg-branch 1911, stpd-kettle-river-branch 1890.

1872 NP lease of the LS&M: did NP crews run the St. Paul - Duluth trains, and until when? Poor's Manual 1873-77 or the Minnesota Railroad Commissioner reports would settle whether lsm-st-paul-duluth splits at 1872.
Exact day of the 1900 NP purchase.

Branch passenger starts in the St. P&D era (Stillwater, Grantsburg, Cloquet) and branch passenger ends (Stillwater 1915-1951, Taylors Falls 1902-1948, Grantsburg 1911-1951, Cloquet after 1951, Kettle River after 1890): an 1880s-1930s Official Guide would settle most.
Heritage railroad start 1980 vs 1981; Minnesota Zephyr start 1985 vs 1986.
All headway_min and avg_speed_kmh values are estimates except np-st-paul-carlton's two round trips (chicagorailfan, 1956).
metadata.open_question_other_layers: northern_pacific.geojson np-duluth-staples (drawn 1873-1970) draws its Duluth - Carlton leg on the Willard Munger State Trail, i.e. the 1886-88 Duluth Short Line: a Rule 2 later-alignment error for 1873-1887 (NP trains then used the LS&M / St. P&D via Fond du Lac), and by the July 1950 Guide (Table 5) the Staples trains ran Duluth - Superior - Pokegama on the NP's own line, so for part of its span the drawn route is wrong; its geometry_quality does not say so. Not changed here. Its layer metadata also claims a real-traced Duluth - St. Paul segment that no feature draws.

properties.line: Lake Superior and Mississippi: St. Paul – Duluth
properties.speed_source: estimate; no timetable speed checked - unsourced
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror, 2026-11-03) and OpenHistoricalMap, routed with opstrace.py. No old_railway_operator tag in the 44.9,-93.2 to 46.85,-91.95 box names this road or NP (only 9 ways tagged BN); OpenHistoricalMap supplies ways named/operated "Lake Superior and Mississippi Railroad", used at full weight.
properties.geometry_quality: 152.6 mi drawn St. Paul - Duluth against ~155 mi documented (GLOBE-1890's figure for the later Short Line route; the 1870 route via Fond du Lac was of similar length, not separately measured). St. Paul - Carlton: Traced 131.2 mi St. Paul Union Depot - Carlton against 131 mi documented (FOWLER-MN mileposts 10 -> 141). 120.2 mi on OpenHistoricalMap ways attributed to the Lake Superior and Mississippi, 9.2 mi on untagged OHM rail and 1.9 mi on untagged OSM rail; no straight-line legs by the router. Every timetable town from White Bear to Barnum is within 0.8 km of the line (St. Paul Union Depot 0.5 km). OHM's line is a hand-drawn historical alignment, coarser than OSM track (about one vertex per 0.7 km); between St. Paul and White Bear it follows the old St. P&D grade (Bruce Vento Trail / Minnesota Commercial corridor), NOT the Gateway State Trail, which is the ex-Wisconsin Central. Hinckley - Carlton is the 1870 grade, now the Willard Munger State Trail (abandoned 1977). Carlton - Thomson (1.2 mi) is HAND-PLACED: three points along the straight Munger Trail grade, because OHM's 'LS&M' way east of Carlton actually bends south onto the NP's Carlton - Superior (Pokegama) line and the router followed it; the hand line is a straight approximation of a straight grade. Thomson - Fond du Lac - Boy Scout Landing (8.4 mi) is APPROXIMATED: four straight legs through hand-placed points (Thomson, the Forbay reservoir, the river bank east of it, Fond du Lac, Boy Scout Landing). The 1870 grade through the St. Louis River gorge (Jay Cooke State Park) is not mapped as a railway in OSM or OHM; OHM's only 'LS&M' way here runs south into Wisconsin on the NP Superior line and was rejected. Boy Scout Landing - New Duluth - Morgan Park - Riverside is traced on the present Lake Superior and Mississippi heritage track, which IS the 1870 alignment (FOWLER-MN 'h'). Riverside - West Duluth - Oneota - Duluth Union Depot follows today's BNSF bayfront track: LATER ALIGNMENT - the 1870s line ran along the same shore but its exact course before the 1880s-1890s yard and dock filling is not checked. Straight legs in this feature: Carlton - Thomson 1.2 mi (hand-placed on a straight grade) and Thomson - Fond du Lac - Boy Scout Landing 8.4 mi. Drawn on the 1870 Fond du Lac alignment, NOT the 1888 Short Line.

segments.note: Lake Superior and Mississippi Railroad, the first rail link between the Twin Cities and Lake Superior: St. Paul - White Bear - Forest Lake - Wyoming - Rush City - Pine City - Hinckley - Finlayson - Moose Lake - Carlton (Northern Pacific Junction) - Thomson - Fond du Lac - Duluth. Final spike at Thomson 1 Aug 1870 and the first train reached Duluth from St. Paul the same day (stlouisriver.org); daily service from 22 Aug 1870 (Zenith City, title only). Ends 1877, when the company was reorganized as the St. Paul and Duluth (month not established) - trains continued under that name (lsm feature ends, stpd features begin). Steam from the start. UNRESOLVED: the Northern Pacific leased the LS&M in 1872 (trains.com); whether NP crews actually ran these trains, and when the lease lapsed (NP failed 1873, receivership 30 Jun 1875), is not established, so the whole span is drawn in LS&M colour. If the lease is shown to have been operative this feature splits 1870-1872 LS&M / 1872-? NP. Partial St. Paul - White Bear service before Aug 1870 is plausible but not checked and not drawn. headway_min 1440 (one daily train each way) is an estimate from 'daily service'; the actual number of trains is not sourced.

segments.note: St. Paul and Duluth Railroad, the LS&M reorganized in 1877: St. Paul (Union Depot) - White Bear - Forest Lake - Wyoming - North Branch - Rush City - Pine City - Hinckley - Finlayson - Willow River - Moose Lake - Barnum - Carlton - Thomson, with through trains running on to Duluth over the original Fond du Lac line until c.1886-88 (stpd-thomson-fond-du-lac-duluth) and then over the Duluth Short Line (stpd-duluth-short-line). GLOBE-1890: 'Mainline, St. Paul to Duluth 155'; GLOBE-1884: 295,470 passengers carried system-wide in 1884. In 1894 the 'Duluth Limited', train No. 4, was the Hinckley-fire rescue train (context). Ends 1900 on purchase by the Northern Pacific (day not found). headway_min 720 is an estimate - no St. P&D timetable count was checked.

segments.note: Northern Pacific, ex-St. P&D main line St. Paul - White Bear Lake - Forest Lake - Wyoming - Stacy - North Branch - Harris - Rush City - Pine City - Hinckley - Friesland - Groningen - Finlayson - Willow River - Sturgeon Lake - Moose Lake - Barnum - Carlton, from the 1900 purchase. The Feb 1952 Official Guide (Table 6 'Duluth Short Line', schedules 14 Jan 1951) indexes Stacy, Harris, North Branch, Finlayson, Sturgeon Lake, Willow River, Barnum, Groningen, Friesland and Hinckley under 'Northern Pacific, 6' without a freight-only dagger, so the 1951 NP trains still ran this route via Moose Lake, not the GN's Sandstone line. Trains 65/66, the last NP Twin Cities - Duluth trains, were discontinued 4 Jan 1967 (Star Tribune 3 Jan 1967 as cited by the Hinckley and Finlayson station articles - the clipping itself was not seen). Burlington Northern (1970) never ran a regular passenger train here and Amtrak never used this line. headway_min 720 = two round trips, from chicagorailfan's 1956 listing (NP 61/62/65/66 in 1942 and 1956); other years not sourced.

segments.note: Original 1870 LS&M line, St. P&D era: Thomson - Greeley - Fond du Lac - New Duluth - Boat Club - Spirit Lake - Riverside - West Duluth Junction - Duluth, carrying the St. Paul - Duluth through trains. FOWLER-MN lists Fond du Lac in the 1875 Guide and Spirit Lake in 1876. The end year is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known ending: the through trains moved to the Duluth Short Line, built 1886-88 (cutoff and St. Louis River bridge dated 1888 - johnmarvigbridges, via search summary), so they certainly used this line until some point between 1886 and 1888. Do not extend without evidence. Post-1888 local service (Fond du Lac - Thomson ended 1894 when a trestle burned; 'service to Fond du Lac ended in 1925', not stated to be passenger - both second-hand from a now-dead Zenith City page) has no confirmed passenger year and is NOT drawn. headway_min is an estimate.

segments.note: Northern Pacific trains over the Duluth Short Line after the 1900 purchase. FOWLER-MN dates West Duluth Junction in the 1902 Official Guide; the Feb 1952 Guide's Table 6 (schedules 14 Jan 1951) prints a column Carlton 141 - Thomson 143 - West Duluth - Twentieth Avenue 161 - Duluth (Un. Depot) 162 with times, so passenger trains used the Short Line in Jan 1951 (OCR reading, confidence medium - a bus footnote sits nearby). Do not extend without evidence. SOURCE CONFLICT: a search summary of a now-dead Zenith City article says the Short Line 'ceased operation in October, 1949', which the 1951 Guide contradicts; unresolved. headway_min is an estimate.

segments.note: Taylors Falls and Lake Superior RR, Wyoming - Chisago City - Lindstrom - Center City - Shafer - Franconia - Taylors Falls; first run 9 Nov 1880 and passengers rode the first train into Taylors Falls ([BYWAY]). Sold to (BYWAY) or leased by (GLOBE-1890/1896) the St. P&D in 1882; the operator in 1880-82 is not established and is presumed St. P&D. west2k (from 1917 NP valuation reports) dates a Taylors Falls passenger station from 1880 and a converted house in use as one from May 1881 through 1902. Ends 1900 on NP purchase. headway_min is an estimate.

segments.note: Knife Falls branch, Carlton (Northern Pacific Junction) - Scanlon - Cloquet. chicagorailfan lists NP mixed trains 731/734 Duluth - Cloquet in 1942; the Feb 1952 Guide's Table 8 'Duluth-Superior-Carlton-Cloquet' (schedules 16 Jul 1950) prints times at Carlton, Scanlon and Cloquet with the footnote 'Freight trains, may carry male adult passengers' - i.e. a MIXED train, the thin end of passenger service, counted under Rule 1. [OPEN] at both ends: 1942 is the first and 1951 the last CONFIRMED year, not a start or an end - the branch was operated by Dec 1884 (GLOBE-1884) but no St. P&D or earlier NP passenger year is confirmed, and no source dates the end. Do not extend without evidence. Through running Duluth - Superior - Carlton used the NP's own Superior line (not drawn here). headway_min is an estimate.
